from rich.highlighter import ReprHighlighter
from rich.console import Console
from io import StringIO

console = Console(file=StringIO(), force_terminal=True)
highlighter = ReprHighlighter()
url = "https://example.com/~user"
# The ReprHighlighter uses a RegexHighlighter. 
# We want to see if it recognizes the tilde in the URL.
# We can check the result of highlighter.highlight(url)
# but that returns a list of Text objects.
# A simpler way is to use console.print and check if it's highlighted (colored).
# However, checking for colors in StringIO depends on the console settings.
# Let's just use highlighter.highlight and see if the whole URL is one Text object with a style.

result = highlighter.highlight(url)
# CLAIM 1: URL with tilde should be highlighted as a single URL
# If not highlighted correctly, it might be split into multiple parts or not have the 'url' style.
assert len(result) == 1 and result[0].style == "url", repr(result)
EOF

from rich.highlighter import ReprHighlighter
from rich.text import Text

highlighter = ReprHighlighter()
url = "https://example.com/~user"
text = Text(url)
highlighter.highlight(text)

# The ReprHighlighter's regex for URL is:
# r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#]*)"
# Note that '~' is NOT in the character class.

# If the URL contains a tilde, it should not match the regex entirely.
# Let's check the spans.
# If it fails, the tilde will cause the match to stop or not match at all.
# For "https://example.com/~user", it might match "https://example.com/" and then stop.

assert len(text.spans) == 1 and text.spans[0].start == 0 and text.spans[0].end == len(url), repr(text)
EOF
